label: thm-hausdorff-iff-the-diagonal-is-closed
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The empty space (X = ∅) yields an empty product and empty diagonal, which is closed; Hausdorffness holds vacuously. A singleton space also satisfies both sides vacuously. In every non-Hausdorff space the diagonal cannot be closed, because the backward direction would force separation of the inseparable pair. The proof uses only the explicit definitional separation in the forward direction and the basis‑relative closure characterisation in the reverse direction; neither spends any choice principle. Both implications are logically valid for all topological spaces carrying the product topology on the square.
